issues.legal_issue: A probate court determines whether the document was duly executed and attested by a testator of sound disposing mind, rather than whether a particular bequest in it is valid.
material_facts: The probate application was rejected in part because the disposition dedicating property to a deity was considered void for uncertainty and therefore not a will.
The will also made provision for the testator’s daughter.
The Supreme Court considered the validity of the bequest to be outside the probate court’s inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The uncertainty or invalidity of a particular bequest is not a proper ground for refusing probate; the probate court must decide due execution and attestation and the testator’s sound disposing mind.
issues.legal_principle: The probate court’s inquiry is confined to whether the document is the deceased person’s will, duly executed and attested in accordance with law, and whether the testator had a sound disposing mind at execution. Section 2(h) of the Indian Succession Act defines a will, but does not make the validity of each bequest part of the probate inquiry. The Court rejected the lower courts’ reliance on Phundan Lal v. Arya Prithi Nidhi Sabha, 33 All 793, to treat uncertainty in a disposition as a reason to deny probate.

predicates.probate_proceeding: A party is asking a court to grant probate of a document asserted to be a deceased person’s will.
predicates.objection_concerns_validity_of_bequest: An objection to probate alleges that a gift or other disposition in the will is invalid or uncertain.

issues.definition: When probate is sought and the objection concerns a bequest’s validity, the court confines its inquiry to execution, attestation, and the testator’s capacity.

issues.legal_issue: A will’s due execution may be established by credible testimony from an attesting witness, and the witness’s evidence cannot be rejected solely on the circumstances relied on in this case.
material_facts: An attesting witness testified about the will’s due execution and the testator’s testamentary capacity.
The trial judge, who saw the witness testify, believed that evidence and found that the will had been duly executed and that the testator had a sound disposing mind.

The High Court rejected the witness’s evidence based on the will being unregistered, the disposition being considered unnatural, the absence of a temple during the testator’s lifetime, the witness’s professional and personal association with the executor’s family, and alleged family discord.

The Supreme Court found those circumstances insufficient to justify disbelieving the witness; it noted, among other things, that a will need not be registered, that the will provided for the daughter, and that evidence showed the family disputes had been composed.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in rejecting the attesting witness’s evidence on the stated grounds; the appeal was allowed and probate was directed to issue.
issues.legal_principle: In a probate case, due execution and testamentary capacity must be proved, and the credibility of an attesting witness is assessed on the evidence and surrounding circumstances. Non-registration of a will does not, by itself, support an inference against genuineness because the law does not require registration of a will. The circumstances identified by the High Court did not justify rejecting testimony accepted by the trial judge who had seen the witness. No earlier case was relied on for this evidentiary conclusion.

rule.if: probate_appeal and attesting_witness_testified_to_execution and trial_judge_credited_attesting_witness and sound_disposing_mind_found and appellate_rejection_based_on_nonregistration_or_disposition_or_delayed_temple_or_association_or_family_discord

predicates.probate_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the grant or refusal of probate.
predicates.attesting_witness_testified_to_execution: A witness who attested the will testified about its execution.
predicates.trial_judge_credited_attesting_witness: The trial judge who observed the witness accepted the witness’s testimony.
predicates.sound_disposing_mind_found: The trial court found that the testator had a sound disposing mind when the will was executed.
predicates.appellate_rejection_based_on_nonregistra: The appellate court rejected the witness’s evidence on grounds such as non-registration, the character or timing of the disposition, the witness’s associations, or family discord.

issues.definition: In a probate appeal, when an attesting witness supports execution, the trial judge credits the witness, capacity is found, and the appellate rejection rests on the listed circumstances, execution and capacity are accepted for probate.
